reuse.why: All month-wide actions share the new category selector and reuse existing budget, sheet, batching, and undo abstractions, although income eligibility remains caller-owned.

duplication.why: The repeated category queries are consolidated, but the new action repeats the income-mode exclusion already present in the other month-wide actions.

placement.why: Category selection and budget calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, while typed method registration and undo wrapping follow the existing app.ts layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their method registration, and focused tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selector gives future exclusion changes a clear home, with only the repeated income eligibility checks weakening central ownership.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six month-wide actions call getMonthWideBudgetCategories, and the new method uses the existing mutation and undo wrappers.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining repeated income-mode guard is explicit rather than renamed or reshaped to conceal duplication.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideBudgetCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories option; fixed-group and template exclusions remain shared, with no caller-specific exceptions or bypasses.
